transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-17
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood CSM), Maya Patel (Glacier CTO), Liam O'Connor (Glacier ML), Rashid Ahmed (Glacier SRE), Sofia Nguyen (Product)

Summary:
- Quick review of last week's changes (prefix TTL bump, cache instrumentation)
- Current KV cache hit = ~18% measured in staging; prefix cache hit ~32%
- Discussed root causes: prompt variance, user-specific tokens in prompts, non-deterministic whitespace, and recent client-side prompt concatenation
- Agreed experiments: deterministic prompt hashing, canonical prompt templates, increase prefix TTL from 5m->15m for select routes, run 24h replay + benchmark

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Okay, everyone, thanks for joining, this is the weekly caching sync. quick rundown of agenda, priya's got the metrics, then we'll go into the prompt reuse strategy and action items.
[00:18] Priya Singh: Hi all. So, quick updates - we rolled the prefix TTL bump on monday to the staging pool, you can see the prefix hit jumped modestly, from 26 to about 32 percent on most routes. KV cache though still low, around eighteen percent, which is below what we expected.
[00:34] Maya Patel: Eighteen, ok. Is that across all customers or just our traffic?
[00:40] Priya Singh: That's scoped to your traffic replay in staging, based on the CSV you gave us. global patterns differ, but for your workload the KV hit is 18. A lot of the misses are from prompt-level variance - user names, timestamps, session tokens, sometimes the client is appending extra context.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: We saw that too; our UI seeds the prompt with a short history and sometimes the last message includes a UUID. We were hoping caching would handle that, but obviously it doesn't if the prompt isn't canonicalized.
[01:20] Priya Singh: Exactly. The cache keys are currently a simple sha256 of the full prompt string, including whitespace and punctuation. So small diffs blow the key. We recommend deterministic hashing after normalization - lowercase, strip extra whitespace, redact user ids or replace them with stable placeholders.
[01:44] Alex Chen: Quick Q on prefix vs KV - for folks not deep in the runtime, the prefix cache is more forgiving because it's keyed on the prefix up to the KV materialization point, while the KV cache needs exact matches to the key, right?
[01:58] Priya Singh: Yeah, prefix benefit is you get partial reuse of KV cache and less brittle matches, but it doesn't save as many tokens in some flows. KV is highest win but requires strong reuse.
[02:12] Rashid Ahmed: Any risk of privacy issues with replacing user ids? We need to ensure no PII ends up in logs or cache keys.
[02:21] Priya Singh: Good call. We recommend pseudonymization - replace user ids with a stable hash using your KMS-derived salt, so Redwood doesn't receive raw PII. Also we can support client-side hashing if you prefer. We'll document patterns.
[02:38] Liam O'Connor: If we canonicalize prompts, what hit rate should we target?
[02:43] Priya Singh: From other customers, after normalization and dedupe, we've seen KV hit climb to 40-60% on high reuse routes. For you, realistic target 40% within a week of the replay. Prefix may go to 50+ percent depending on route distributions.
[03:03] Alex Chen: We also ran a quick A/B with batching parameters; small increase in batch window helped throughput but raised p95 slightly. we'll provide the exact numbers.
[03:15] Diego Ramos: note - batching tradeoffs; you should pick latency or cost primarily for the critical route.
[03:21] Maya Patel: Our priority is p95 sub-second for search assistant flows. Cost matters but latency first.
[03:28] Priya Singh: Understood. For that route we should be conservative on batching and focus on KV improvements first.
[03:36] Liam O'Connor: About instrumentation - can Redwood surface per-prompt hash distribution and top-100 near-miss keys so we can see similar prompts that missed?
[03:47] Priya Singh: Yes, we can add a report - top near-miss clusters and token-level savings estimate. we'll include that in the replay deliverable.
[03:55] Rashid Ahmed: Also need to validate eviction policy under burst traffic. We saw evictions spike during load tests last week.
[04:03] Priya Singh: Eviction was tuned to LRU with a slight priority for prefix entries. For the next run we'll instrument evictions by route and by request, and bump reserved memory for KV in the dedicated pool if needed.
[04:18] Alex Chen: Let's capture concrete experiments: 1) deterministic prompt hashing and normalization, 2) replay 24h with hashing, 3) prefix TTL extended to 15m on these five routes, 4) run benchmark p95/p99 after replay. anyone object?
[04:33] Maya Patel: Sounds good. One question - how do we handle user-specific tokens in generated text? If we pseudonymize in keys, generated output must still map back.
[04:42] Priya Singh: Right - two options: client-side tokenization + placeholder substitution before sending, then substitute back on the client when rendering; or server-side pseudonymization with KMS lookup at render time. Customer preference?
[04:56] Liam O'Connor: We'll likely do client-side replacement for now, faster and avoids server-held PII.
[05:02] Diego Ramos: I'll note that in the runbook.
[05:08] Alex Chen: Timeline check - Priya, can you get the hashing patch and config snippets out by thursday (2025-06-19)?
[05:15] Priya Singh: Yes, I can. I'll also include the normalization rules and an example client patch.
[05:21] Liam O'Connor: We'll run the 24h replay starting Friday and send results by Tuesday morning.
[05:28] Maya Patel: We'll also review security docs; Alex, please include SOC2 section and KMS notes.
[05:33] Alex Chen: Will do.
[05:36] Rashid Ahmed: small nit - you mentioned prefix TTL bump; what's the delta in memory usage?
[05:41] Priya Singh: On staging it's about a 12% increase in cache footprint for those routes, but evictions didn't spike proportionally. We'll send the memory delta report.
[05:50] Sofia Nguyen: For product planning, if KV hits reach 40% that materially reduces cost per request - can you share a modeled savings figure so we can include it in our internal review?
[06:00] Alex Chen: Yes we'll provide modeled cost savings given token reduction and hit-rate scenarios.
[06:06] Priya Singh: Also recommend short-term dedupe: if two prompts are identical after normalization within X minutes, treat as same key - that'll help conversational reuse where users repeat the same question.
[06:20] Liam O'Connor: That makes sense. We'll enable dedupe for the assistant route.
[06:25] Alex Chen: Any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:29] Maya Patel: No blockers. main concern is privacy and making sure substitutions are reversible client-side.
[06:35] Priya Singh: We'll document patterns and a sample client lib for substitution.
[06:41] Alex Chen: Okay, recap of action items in chat and we'll meet same time next week. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
